title: Fluency: measuring a rise or a fall

families.skill: find a percentage rise or fall
families.prompt: A share {verb} from £{old:dp2} to £{new:dp2}. By what percentage did it {noun}?

wrong.line: You divided by the new price. A change is measured against the original price, £{old:dp2}.
That is the new price as a percentage of the old. Take the change, £{diff:dp2}, over the old price.
The {noun} is £{diff:dp2}, but pounds are not per cent. Divide it by the original £{old:dp2}.

solution: The {noun} is the gap between the prices, £{diff:dp2}.
Divide by the original price: ${diff} \div {old} = {key}$, which is {p}%.

families.skill: find a daily return from two closes
families.prompt: A stock closes at £{y:dp2} on Monday and at £{t:dp2} on Tuesday. What is its daily return?

wrong.line: Check the sign: a rise is a positive return and a fall is a negative one.
You divided by Tuesday's close. A return is measured against the earlier close, £{y:dp2}.

solution: Divide by Monday's close: ${diff} \div {y} = {key}$, a return of {r}%.
